summary: ORBITAL is a zero-scroll, browser-based space mission design simulator built with pure HTML, Tailwind CSS, modular ES6 JavaScript, and Three.js (running entirely client-side without Node.js). Players act as aerospace engineers for Team Zero.Syntaxx, configuring seven interdependent satellite subsystems—Imaging, Power, Propulsion, Target Orbit, Communication, Thermal Management, and Radiation Shielding—against live mass, budget, power, propellant, thermal, and radiation telemetry. After a 3-step pre-flight diagnostic review, players launch their custom spacecraft in a 3D orbital simulation featuring multi-stage rocket ascent, fairing separation, and either a successful orbital downlink or a deep-space drift failure, culminating in a 100-point engineering scorecard and debrief.
details:
ORBITAL is an interactive, browser-based space mission engineering game built by Team Zero.Syntaxx. Putting players in the seat of an aerospace systems architect, the game challenges them to design, validate, and launch an Earth-observation satellite under strict real-world engineering trade-offs.

Players configure seven core spacecraft subsystems—Imaging, Power, Propulsion, Target Orbit, Communication, Thermal Management, and Radiation Shielding—while monitoring live telemetry for mass, budget, power balance, delta-v propellant margins, heat dissipation, and radiation reliability. After running a pre-flight engineering diagnostic to catch design flaws and bottlenecks, players initiate a real-time 3D orbital simulation powered by Three.js. Depending on their engineering choices, the spacecraft either executes a clean multi-stage launch into stable Earth orbit for data downlink, or suffers a dynamic deep-space insertion failure. Finally, a 100-point scoring engine evaluates scientific yield, resource efficiency, operational performance, and reliability, offering actionable feedback to optimize future missions.
